title: Uncovering the structure of self-regulation through data-driven ontology discovery
authors: Ian W. Eisenberg, Patrick G. Bissett, A. Zeynep Enkavi, Jamie Li, David P. MacKinnon, Lisa A. Marsch, Russell A. Poldrack
caption_short: Schematic of the adaptive letter n-back: letters appear one at a time and the participant presses one key when the letter matches the one N back (case ignored); N changes between blocks with performance.
notes: Drawn by us: none of the papers describing this dataset has a task figure for this task. Eisenberg et al. 2019 (Nat Commun, CC BY 4.0) has eight figures, all analysis figures (Fig. 1a only lists task names, including 'Adaptive N-back'); Enkavi et al. 2019 (PNAS) shows reliability results only; Eisenberg et al. 2018 (Behav Res Ther 101:46-57) lists the tasks in a table without figures; the Experiment Factory paper (Sochat et al. 2016, Front Psychol 7:610) shows software diagrams only. The task details in the schematic are taken from the task code that ran the study (github.com/expfactory/expfactory-experiments, MIT licence, adaptive_n_back/experiment.js): letters b d g t v in both cases, 500 ms display, 2000 ms response window, 20 adaptive blocks of 20 + N letters with round(20/3) = 7 targets, starting N = 2, N + 1 after fewer than 3 mistakes and N - 1 after more than 5 (no decrease below 1), left arrow = match, down arrow = otherwise. The example sequence g G v T b t b with N = 2 is the one in the task's own instructions. Rendered with Pillow (DejaVu Sans) at 1400 px width, the same size as the digit-span schematic.
